clue.text: Stranger to Scots nearly abandoned steam

definitions.note: a noun standing for an adjective: the answer describes someone with the heat or agitation of steam, the opposite of cool

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: in Scots, unco is a noun meaning a stranger
something old has been abandoned, put aside as worn out

explanation.surface: A Scottish visitor nearly gave up on a steam engine or a steam bath.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCO plus OL(d) spells UNCOOL; the setter takes it as the opposite of cool, so all steamed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uncool literally means not cool, so the setter equates it with being hot and agitated, all steamed up.

clue.text: Fold completely over women’s high praise

blocks.note: when time is up, it is completely over
W is the abbreviation for women
the setter uses rap as a word for acclaim, as in a good rap

explanation.surface: A woman folds something over completely and is much praised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as a noun meaning a fold or wrapping, an old term for something wrapped up.

clue.text: Damage and impair variable flavour of ale

blocks.note: what's the damage? asks what it costs
to mar is to spoil or impair
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Something spoils the changeable taste of a pint of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Damage reads as harm, but it is the slang sense of price.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is an aromatic herb that brewers once used to give ale its taste, hence the alternative name alecost.

clue.text: For musicians or fabulous bard (not Norse)

indicators.note: not means without, so the bracketed letter is removed

blocks.note: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard of James Macpherson's poems
N is the abbreviation for Norse

explanation.surface: For musicians, or perhaps for a legendary poet who isn't Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means belonging to fable: Ossian's poems were largely invented by Macpherson.
explanation.definitionFit: In a score, ossia marks an alternative passage the performer may play instead, so musicians read it as a word meaning alternatively.

clue.text: Open country means room to move

blocks.note: lee is a variant of lea, open grassland
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Wide-open countryside gives plenty of space to roam.
explanation.walkthrough: Means looks like the link word, but it supplies WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is freedom of action or margin for manoeuvre, originally a ship's sideways drift.

clue.text: Comparatively dissolute sort off the grub

blocks.note: first meaning: more fast, where fast means wild and pleasure-seeking
second meaning: a person who goes without food for a time

explanation.surface: A debauched type who has lost his appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast in the old sense of loose-living takes a comparative; the same letters name one who fasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast means dissipated, so its comparative is more dissipated; separately, anyone abstaining from food is someone who fasts.

clue.text: Civil war general’s frequently with acting staff sergeant, say

blocks.note: fr. is the abbreviation for frequently
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a rank
a staff sergeant is one example of a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A general in a civil war often has a sergeant acting as his aide.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Franco led the Nationalist forces in the Spanish Civil War and then ruled Spain as dictator.

clue.text: Parent’s holding up nothing in gold sheep

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
in a down clue, the piece holding something up sits underneath it

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
O looks like a zero, nothing
dad is a parent, with its apostrophe s kept

explanation.surface: A parent props up a gold sheep holding nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The parent supports the rest from below in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The aoudad, or Barbary sheep, is a wild sheep of North Africa, so the plural means sheep.

clue.text: So, about university female becoming ascetic?

definitions.note: an adjective meaning of the Sufis; the question mark flags that ascetic is only one aspect of it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the others

blocks.note: sic is Latin for so, thus
U is the abbreviation for university
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A female student turns to a life of self-denial.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufic relates to Sufism, the Islamic mystical tradition known for asceticism, hence the hedging question mark.

clue.text: European lecturer to harangue voters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
lect. is an abbreviation for lecturer
to orate is to speechify or harangue

explanation.surface: A European academic lectures the public at length.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the whole body of people entitled to vote in an election.

clue.text: Fuss about what’s at the heart of creating shop

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, so only its middle letters are kept
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: a rout is an old word for a fuss or disturbance
the two central letters of an eight-letter word

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper causes a commotion over what's central to the business.
explanation.walkthrough: Shop looks like a noun but is the slang verb for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police, as is to rat out.

clue.text: Dramatic wizard beside me, royally rolling in it

indicators.note: beside places the second piece directly next to the first, so they are joined end to end

blocks.note: Prospero is the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest
a monarch uses the royal we, so me becomes us

explanation.surface: A stage magician, speaking like a king, boasts of being wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in it is an idiom for having plenty of money, which is the state of wealthy, thriving people.

clue.text: One such as Smiley let home run down

indicators.note: a run that has broken down is wrecked, so these words are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer or baseball player let a run home slip away, like a famous spy.
explanation.walkthrough: George Smiley is le Carré's spymaster, who in Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy tracks down a Soviet double agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy planted inside an organisation, and Smiley's task in Tinker Tailor is to hunt one down.

clue.text: Old self-service where each gets covered in batter

indicators.note: something covered in another thing sits wholly inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to buffet is to batter or strike repeatedly
EA is the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: At an old-fashioned self-service counter, everything is dipped in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: Batter suggests fish-fry coating, but here it is the verb to beat. BEAUFFET is an obsolete spelling of buffet.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a meal where diners help themselves, and this spelling is an archaic form of that word.

clue.text: Go off one’s parathas

definitions.note: parathas are one kind of the answer, so this is a definition by example

blocks.note: food that goes off begins to rot
one is I in Roman numerals, with the apostrophe s kept as S

explanation.surface: Someone's flatbreads have gone stale.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratha is a layered, pan-fried Indian flatbread, one particular variety of the broader family of Indian breads.

clue.text: Discontinued senior officer’s club of a certain sort

blocks.note: dis. is the dictionary abbreviation for discontinued; that the whole answer also sits at the front of this word is a coincidence the setter enjoys
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A retired commanding officer's private members' club has shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an officers' club; the answer is a nightclub for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot where people dance to recorded music is one particular kind of club, hence the vague 'of a certain sort'.

clue.text: Source of info from dancer not available ahead of compliance

indicators.note: ahead of places the earlier pieces in front of the next one in the sequence

blocks.note: an alma (or almah) is an Egyptian dancing girl
N/A is the usual abbreviation for not available
C is a dictionary abbreviation for compliance

explanation.surface: A dancer who cannot attend is asked to cooperate before giving information.
explanation.walkthrough: ALMA, the Egyptian dancing girl, is a word found mainly in Chambers and in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly reference book of calendars, tides and statistics is a standard place people look things up.

clue.text: Conclude racket is squeezed

blocks.note: to close is to bring to an end
a racket is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: Ending a noisy protest means the crowd gets crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hemmed in on every side leaves little space, which is the cramped sense of squeezed.

clue.text: Barrow boy is quiet at dawn

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
dawn is early in the day

explanation.surface: A street trader keeps quiet first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow boy is a London street seller working from a handcart; a pearly is a costermonger in a pearl-buttoned costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists pearly as a noun for a London costermonger, the traditional street trader selling from a barrow.

clue.text: Spinach in prescribed course such as tratt serves

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: a lane is a set course, as for a runner or swimmer
saag is spinach in Indian cooking, also spelt sag

explanation.surface: An Italian restaurant serves a set menu with spinach in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A tratt is short for trattoria, an informal Italian restaurant; SAG is an Indian-menu word for spinach.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta baked with sauce is a staple dish on any Italian trattoria menu.

clue.text: Informed study backing block of, say, ninety-nine shares

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the joined words are read from end to start

blocks.note: to be told is to be informed
to do a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: An informed piece of research supports buying shares in an unusual quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: On stock markets, trades are normally in round hundreds; a parcel of fewer, like ninety-nine, is the trading term for an irregular holding.

clue.text: Hacker’s high point of gaff involving personnel dept?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around and including, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: the peak is the upper outer corner of a gaff sail
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A computer intruder's best moment came from a blunder involving the human resources office.
explanation.walkthrough: Gaff looks like slang for a home or a blunder, but it is the spar of a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A phreak originally broke into telephone systems, and the word extends to anyone breaking into computer networks illegally.

clue.text: Ha’penny I accepted with a bit of loose change in Dhaka

definitions.text: bit of loose change in Dhaka

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: posh is old slang for money, specifically a halfpenny
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a halfpenny with some spare coins in Bangladesh.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha'penny was an old British coin worth half a penny. Posh looks like an adjective but is old slang for one.
explanation.definitionFit: The poisha is a minor coin of Bangladesh, a hundredth of a taka, so small change in its capital.

clue.text: Tanka composed about sword

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged anew

blocks.note: taken as written
a. is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A Japanese poem written on the subject of a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanka is a short Japanese poem, which pairs neatly with a Japanese sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A katana is the long curved single-edged blade carried by samurai warriors in Japan.

clue.text: Absent and shipwrecked hero’s on terra firma

indicators.note: a wrecked ship is broken apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: A is the register abbreviation for absent
the letters of the word with its S

explanation.surface: A castaway hero, missing at sea, has made it to dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra firma is Latin for solid ground, and being on the beach rather than at sea means being on land.

clue.text: Garment put out to dry fell

blocks.note: an aba is a loose sleeveless Arab cloak
to ted is to spread mown grass out to dry

explanation.surface: A coat hung outside to dry falls down.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like a noun, a hill, but it is the past tense meaning went down.
explanation.definitionFit: When wind or a fever abates, it lessens or subsides, as something does when its level falls.

clue.text: Society removed from poet’s old writ

indicators.note: removed from means taken out of, so one letter is dropped from the longer word

blocks.note: an elegist is a poet who writes elegies
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A poet expelled from a literary society carries an ancient legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegit was a historic English writ of execution letting a creditor take a debtor's goods and land until paid.

clue.text: Teacher of the Old Testament, an imitator of English essayist

blocks.note: Eli is the priest who taught the young Samuel in the Old Testament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A biblical teacher imitates an English writer of essays.
explanation.walkthrough: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, the English essayist; an Elian writes in his manner.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an Elian is a follower or imitator of Lamb's style in the Essays of Elia.

clue.text: Particularly profound American not after girl from the east

indicators.note: across clues read west to east, so coming from the east means read right to left

blocks.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
not after means before, as in finished by noon
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An American, ahead of a girl from the Orient, is especially deep.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes the very deep ocean zones, and figuratively anything bottomless or extremely deep.

clue.text: Sabbath and oddly hourly opening for Netanya’s synagogues

indicators.note: oddly keeps the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth
the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for Sabbath
its first, third and fifth letters
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Every hour on the Sabbath, the synagogues of an Israeli city open their doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Netanya is a coastal city in Israel. SHULN is the Yiddish plural of shul.
explanation.definitionFit: Shul is the Yiddish word for a Jewish house of worship, and this is its plural form.

clue.text: Apartment block in Rome wanting tip from scrap plant

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the longer word
the tip of a word is its very first letter

blocks.note: an insula was a Roman block of flats
its opening letter

explanation.surface: An old Roman tenement, with a scrap of ground missing, grows a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: INSULA loses the S supplied by scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Inula is a genus of yellow-flowered daisy-family herbs, including elecampane, so it names a plant.

clue.text: Freeman’s possibly tethered, though not embarrassed

indicators.note: though not means without, so those letters are left out of the longer word
possibly signals one possible arrangement among many, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: A free man may be tied up but feels no shame about it.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens a thete was a member of the lowest class of citizens: free, but poor and without property.

clue.text: Streaked in pompous outfit

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other here

blocks.note: state as an adjective means ceremonial, full of pomp
a rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Someone is striped in a self-important costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Strigate is a botanical and zoological term for marked with narrow lines or bands, which is to say striped.

clue.text: Nice inn with all canned legumes

indicators.note: canned can mean drunk, so these words are in a jumbled state

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel in Nice serves only tinned beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Canned fits the beans so well that it hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannellini are white Italian kidney beans, and beans belong to the pod-bearing plant family of legumes.

clue.text: Are frogs full of English spiders?

definitions.note: the answer is a genus name, so it stands for a group of spiders

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a
Rana is the genus of common frogs
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A question asking whether French people are full of English spiders.
explanation.walkthrough: Frogs looks like slang for the French, but it is the genus RANA. Are is not a verb here but the unit of land area.
explanation.definitionFit: Aranea is the Latin word and a genus name covering the orb-weaving spiders, so it can stand for them.

clue.text: Fellow native is an idler, Compo for instance

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow
nat. is the abbreviation for native

explanation.surface: A college fellow and a local are both lazy, like a famous television layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Compo is the scruffy idler of the long-running BBC Yorkshire comedy Last of the Summer Wine; donnat is Yorkshire dialect for a good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English dialect a donnat is a worthless or idle person, and Compo is a famous fictional example of the type.
